reason: The deemed-complete default genuinely protects the speaker: administrative silence now starts the clock and permits publication rather than suppressing it, and the substantive test is untouched. A 24-hour completeness check cannot harm speakers, because the Commission's failure runs in their favour. One residual flaw: s 8.5(3) measures 48 hours from receipt while s 8.5(5) measures from 'a complete application', which on one reading stretches the outer restraint to 72 hours. Curable by condition.
conditions: In s 8.5(5), measure the 48 hours from receipt of the application (not from deemed completion), so the maximum restraint is 48 hours.
Confine an incomplete determination to the matters listed in s 8.5(2), so repeated 'incomplete' responses cannot extend delay beyond the 5-working-day lead time.
